title: Coefficient tensor product commutes with homogeneous localized module pieces
statement:
Let $R\to S$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings, $A=\bigoplus_{n\geq0}A_n$ a commutative unital graded ring with a unital map $R\to A_0$, and $M=\bigoplus_{i\in\mathbf Z}M_i$ a graded $A$-module, meaning $A_nM_i\subseteq M_{n+i}$. Put $C=S\otimes_RA$, graded by $C_n=S\otimes_RA_n$, and $N=S\otimes_RM$, graded by $N_i=S\otimes_RM_i$, with $C$-action $(s\otimes a)(t\otimes x)=st\otimes ax$. Fix $f\in A_d$, $d>0$, and put $f_S=1\otimes f$. Write $M_f$ and $N_{f_S}$ for module localization at the powers of $f$ and $f_S$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]. For every integer $j$, let $(M_f)_j$ be the $R$-submodule of $M_f$ consisting of fractions $x/f^m$ with $m\geq0$ and $x\in M_{md+j}$, and define $(N_{f_S})_j$ similarly. Equality is the ordinary module-localization relation, so $x/f^m=y/f^n$ if and only if $f^k(f^nx-f^my)=0$ for some $k\geq0$. The displayed subsets are $R$- and $S$-modules respectively, with addition by a common denominator. The rule
$$\lambda_{M,f,j}:S\otimes_R(M_f)_j\xrightarrow{\sim}(N_{f_S})_j,\qquad s\otimes(x/f^m)\longmapsto(s\otimes x)/f_S^m$$
defines an isomorphism of $S$-modules. No flatness, finite generation, boundedness of the grading of $M$, or non-zero-divisor hypothesis on $f$ is imposed.

proof.text: Construct the R-submodule H of homogeneous fractions using a common denominator: multiplying the numerator by f^n shifts its degree by nd, so addition and coefficient scalar multiplication preserve the carrier. Apply lem-sfb-homogeneous-localization-retraction to obtain an R-linear retraction of H → M_f. Tensoring this retraction shows that S⊗H → S⊗M_f is injective, without flatness.

On pure tensors the canonical C-action satisfies (1⊗f)(s⊗x)=s⊗fx. Induction on a preimage under the tensor map S⊗M_i → (M_i).baseChange S shows that f_S shifts these submodules by d. The same common-denominator construction gives K with exactly the required carrier.

Use lem-sfb-localization-scalar-extension-coefficients to obtain the ambient S-linear equivalence e0:S⊗M_f → N_fS with its fraction formula. Its composite g with S⊗H → S⊗M_f maps into K: prove this on pure tensors of homogeneous fractions, then use tensor induction. Restrict g to K. Injectivity follows from the ambient equivalence and the tensored retraction.

For surjectivity take z=y/f_S^m in K, with y in (M_(j+md)).baseChange S. Lift y to S⊗M_(j+md), then induct on that tensor. Zero has preimage zero, s⊗x lifts to s⊗(x/f^m), and sums lift to sums using additivity of fractions with the same denominator. The resulting bijective S-linear map gives the requested equivalence. Its normalized fraction equation is the ambient equation.
